english: Six students $S_{1},S_{2},\ldots,S_{6}$ write a test. For peer review the six answer scripts are redistributed among them, one script to each student, in such a way that no student receives the script written by that student; all such redistributions are equally likely. The probability that $S_{1}$ receives the script of $S_{2}$ and $S_{2}$ receives the script of $S_{1}$ is
hindi: छः विद्यार्थी $S_{1},S_{2},\ldots,S_{6}$ एक परीक्षा देते हैं। परस्पर मूल्यांकन के लिए छः उत्तर-पुस्तिकाएँ उनमें इस प्रकार पुनः वितरित की जाती हैं कि प्रत्येक विद्यार्थी को एक पुस्तिका मिले और किसी भी विद्यार्थी को उसकी स्वयं लिखी पुस्तिका न मिले; ऐसे सभी वितरण समसम्भाव्य हैं। $S_{1}$ को $S_{2}$ की पुस्तिका तथा $S_{2}$ को $S_{1}$ की पुस्तिका मिलने की प्रायिकता है
solution: Favourable: $S_{1}\leftrightarrow S_{2}$ swapped; the other 4 scripts must still avoid their writers $\Rightarrow D_{4}=9$
solution_full: A redistribution is a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,6\}$ ($S_{i}$ receives the script of $S_{\sigma(i)}$) with $\sigma(i)\neq i$ for all $i$, i.e. a derangement. All derangements are equally likely, so the sample space has $D_{6}$ elements.

Favourable outcomes: $\sigma(1)=2$ and $\sigma(2)=1$. Then $\sigma$ maps $\{3,4,5,6\}$ onto itself, and the condition $\sigma(i)\neq i$ for $i=3,4,5,6$ says this restriction is a derangement of four objects: $D_{4}=9$ ways.
(Treating the redistribution as an arbitrary permutation would give $\dfrac{4!}{6!}=\dfrac{1}{30}$, which ignores the condition that defines the sample space.)
originality_note: New: a conditional matching probability in which the sample space itself is the set of derangements and the event (a 2-cycle between two given people) leaves a smaller derangement, so the answer is the ratio D4/D6 (way 5). Closest known: 'probability that no letter goes into the right envelope' (D_n/n!). Different because: the derangement is the condition, not the event, and the event forces a second derangement inside it.

concept_use.Derangements: The sample space is the set of D6 = 265 derangements, and the four remaining scripts must again be deranged (D4 = 9).
concept_use.Derangement and matching probability pro: Matching probability under the condition 'nobody gets their own script': favourable derangements divided by all derangements; the unconditional value 1/30 is the distractor.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed by an independent brute-force enumeration in Python (sympy/itertools), is unique and matches the Answer Plan. Checked that 'redistributions equally likely' fixes the sample space as derangements, that the swap leaves exactly a derangement of the other four, and that 9/265 is at (B) as planned. Changed: replaced 'his or her own script' by 'the script written by that student'.
key_step: Recognising that the sample space is the set of derangements and that the event leaves a derangement of the remaining four.
justification: Two ideas linked: the conditional sample space (derangements, not all permutations) and the reduction of the event to D4; the natural mistake 1/30 is an option. Comparable to the conditional probability 2024-P1-Q2 (L3).
